How the dive works

Each prompt has many correct answers. Type one before your air runs out. If an answer is rejected you can keep trying until the timer ends. Autocorrect is generous: typos and sound-alike spellings get fixed (“cryllion” finds Krill), extra describing words are ignored (“chinese beetle” counts as Beetle, “yellow tomato” as Tomato), and the first word of a long answer is enough when it’s clear which one you mean. If your spelling is close to two answers, you pick.

After you submit, your answer sinks down the tier ladder, slows, and teeters over the next tier before it lands. Press Enter to skip the animation.

Answers are ranked from most to least common. The rarer your answer, the more points you score, and every point takes you 10 metres deeper. A perfect daily dive reaches 7,000 m.

Real answers count even when they’re obscure, scored by how rare they are. In Endless, Rare-or-better answers in a row build a combo that multiplies your depth.

Autocorrect always asks first: if your spelling is close, you get “Do you want it to correct to …?”. Press Enter or Yes to accept, No to retype.

Too Clever is for answers everyone reaches for when they’re trying to be obscure (Liechtenstein, platypus, kumquat). They’re still correct, just not rare.

Some tempting wrong answers are flagged on purpose, like a spider for “insect” or Pluto for “planet”, so you get told exactly why instead of a silent fail. Rankings come from hand-curated lists plus word-frequency data across about 42,000 answers, so the odd valid answer might be missing.
